prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Hospital dispensing/returns. Aliases: Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer.
Morrowglass validates/routes/statuses orders, produces Order Reconciliation Snapshot. Cinderwake reconciles identifiers, authorization, cancellations/duplicates/remainders; holds conflicts, preserves evidence, requires authorized corrections/pharmacy authorization; produces Priority Refill Tote Tag. Clinical Pharmacist produces Dose Exception Review Slip; resolves unclear orders through Morrowglass. Juniper final-checks order/product/strength/form/dose/route/time/patient/label; records approver/time/medication identifiers, requires recorded independent high-risk checks; authorized professionals resolve mismatches before release; produces Batch Release Note. Copperfield checks packaging/lot/expiry, reconciles replenishment, never determines doses; produces Cold Chain Handoff Card. Hospital Courier accepts suitable closed loads, produces Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record.
East Tube Dispatch Console maintains approved route map/segment availability; selects destination/latest-approved-configuration routes, verifies reachability/interlocks/movement conflicts; stale/incomplete/sensor-disconnected status holds dispatch; sends Tube Route Exception Ticket, alerts Copperfield for stalled/unconfirmed transfers. Pneumatic Tube Network reports segment status/progress/delivery; interruptions record capsule/location/time. West Tube Dispatch Console authorizes routing; recovery requires refreshed status/approved route/checks/tests/authorization. Route/temperature records retain timestamps/equipment identifiers.
Charge Nurse sends Cabinet Downtime Notice. South Ward Cabinet Controller reports failures, receives release note, applies approved configuration before compartment enabling. North Ward Cabinet Controller uses tote tag. Both reconcile arrivals, block held/Out of Service dispensing until Ready for Dispense; require current versioned authorized configuration, identity matching, role authentication, inventory/movement accounting; replenishment cannot override clinical restrictions.
Bluejay records temperature/probe/calibration/lot/expiry/access/door/custody history; excursions/probe loss block stock; pharmacist decides release/quarantine/discard; preserve conditions/offline alarms/records until reconnection.
Larkspur locks transactions/confirms nonadministration/escalates; no bypass/substitution. Tallowmere reconciles/segregates/secures returns, produces Return Bin Audit. Receiving staff verify/isolate; unresolved stocking prohibited; Operations coordinates alternatives.

New part:
S205: The South Ward Cabinet Controller checks its local compartment mapping, access rules, and supported medication classes against that configuration.
S206: The cabinet reports Ready for Dispense only after its configuration checks and required device self-tests pass.
S207: The Registered Nurse authenticates at the cabinet and selects the medication associated with the active patient order.
S208: The South Ward Cabinet Controller checks the requested selection against its local authorization rules before unlocking a compartment.
S209: The cabinet records the user, order reference, compartment access, and transaction time for audit review.
S210: Stonewake reviews the received operational record, correlates its equipment identifiers and timestamps with local telemetry, and records an engineering disposition.
S211: The Biomedical Engineer uses the exception ticket to identify the affected path and compare reported symptoms with equipment telemetry.
S212: The Biomedical Engineer checks whether the reported condition is isolated to one device or indicates a broader service risk.
S213: When a hardware or control fault is suspected, the affected equipment is placed in Out of Service status.
S214: The Biomedical Engineer isolates the affected subsystem and performs only the diagnostic steps approved for that equipment.
S215: The IT Operations Specialist investigates authentication, interface, and time-synchronization faults that could affect transaction records.
S216: The Medication Safety Officer reviews any discrepancy that could change medication identity, access control, or patient risk.
S217: The Clinical Pharmacist keeps affected medication unavailable until the relevant order and product checks are repeated successfully.
S218: The Biomedical Engineer records the corrective action, test evidence, and approvals required to return the equipment to operation.
S219: Equipment remains Out of Service until required functional checks pass and the responsible staff approve its return.
S220: Audit records retain timestamps, equipment identifiers, and disposition details to support operational review and investigation.
S221: A cabinet outage is treated as a service incident when the cabinet stops responding, reports a fault, or fails a dispensing check.
S222: The IT Operations Specialist uses the Cabinet Downtime Notice to open a controlled incident record and identify the affected cabinet.
S223: The IT Operations Specialist checks controller status, network connectivity, and recent event logs before attempting recovery.
S224: The IT Operations Specialist records the time the fault was detected and the affected equipment identifier.
S225: The affected North Ward Cabinet Controller or South Ward Cabinet Controller remains Out of Service while the cause is assessed.
S226: The IT Operations Specialist isolates the fault where necessary to prevent repeated dispense requests from reaching an unavailable cabinet.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
